A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeeKer research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between the main text and supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations on UBnormal, ShanghaiTech and MSAD-HR, ablations in Tables 4–10, and qualitative model outputs.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a qualitative UBnormal example showing predicted keypoint distributions and anomaly scores during walking and jumping.

M1.justification: The autoregressive Gaussian keypoint model, masked fully connected architecture, likelihood objective, confidence-weighted anomaly score and frame aggregation remain unchanged. The revised diagrams explain the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate UBnormal and ShanghaiTech, including their human-related subsets, and MSAD-HR. The added walking/jumping visualization illustrates existing UBnormal coverage without introducing a distinct task or evaluation environment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including benchmark Tables 1–3 and the STG-NF smoothing comparison in Table 7. No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, UBnormal validation-based tuning, 24-frame sequences, training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, localization thresholds and Gaussian smoothing settings are retained. The new qualitative example introduces no changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 5 adds a case study comparing predicted distributions and keypoint anomaly scores during normal walking and abnormal jumping. Existing covariance, granularity, confidence, smoothing, ordering, architecture and hyperparameter analyses remain. The smoke case moves from v1 Figure 5 to v3 Appendix C.3/Figure 9.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three runs with variance below 0.05 pp, and retain the keypoint-ordering variance statement. No new uncertainty estimates, statistical tests or seed information appear.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–10 are unchanged. v3 Figure 5 adds qualitative walking/jumping predictions and anomaly-score outputs. v3 also removes Section 5.2's specific 4 pp smoothing statement while retaining Table 7 and the general smoothing findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–23, including the likelihood factorization, optimization derivation and architectural masks in Appendices A–B, retain the same mathematics. The added masking schematic supplies explanation rather than a new definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: autoregressive keypoint density estimation, interpretable confidence-weighted scoring, leading UBnormal/MSAD-HR performance and competitive ShanghaiTech performance.

C2.justification: The new walking/jumping example illustrates the existing explanation that unlikely keypoint locations signal anomalous motion. Interpretations of the ablations and Appendix D's extractor and bias limitations retain their substance. The smoke-related applicability discussion is relocated rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remains the same, including extraction/tracking, optimization settings, confidence filtering, architectural details and the code link. The 0.76 GB memory and under-ten-minute RTX 3090 training disclosures move from Appendix C.3 to C.4.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 62 reference entries and substantive positioning against prior skeleton-based, multimodal and autoregressive approaches. Reference back-page numbers and minor wording change without changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, reorganizes Section 5.2, moves the smoke discussion into Appendix C.3, and adds acknowledgements and a competing-interest declaration. Most prose and the overall scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The visual exposition is substantially revised: v3 adds the masking schematic in Figure 3 and walking/jumping visualization in Figure 5, redraws the training and dependency diagrams, and restyles existing illustrations. Figure 1 moves to the first page, the running visualization becomes single-column, and the smoke figure moves to the appendix. Table contents and structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised method diagrams, explicit masking illustration and new walking/jumping case make conditioning and anomaly scoring easier to understand. Existing evidence remains available, including the relocated smoke example. These are useful explanatory gains, while benchmark results, statistical support, reproducibility details and limitations remain essentially unchanged.
